activity.role: Dynastic political figure and possible ruler
activity.notes: Atotoztli, daughter of Moctezuma I and mother of Axayacatl, Tizoc and Ahuitzotl, was unquestionably central to Mexica dynastic continuity. Later sources differ over whether and how long she ruled after her father. ATLAS therefore records a representative c.1469 political point with disputed confidence and does not assert a formal six-year or twelve-year reign.

sources.title: “Atotoztli” la tlatoani mexica no reconocida — INPI
sources.citation_text: Mexico's INPI summarizes Atotoztli's dynastic importance and the conflicting historical claims that she ruled after Moctezuma I.

sources.title: Aztec women and rulership — RES 47 academic article scan
sources.citation_text: Academic discussion notes that some alphabetic sources posit that Atotoztli inherited the throne and ruled Tenochtitlan for a time, while the evidence remains contested.
